subject.title: fix(apns): reject oversized private key files before JWT signing

question: Should direct APNs private-key path reads adopt the shared 16 KiB credential-file limit, intentionally failing previously accepted oversized files?
rationale: The code and proof support the hardening, but an upgrade-visible fail-closed credential boundary is an explicit maintainer security and compatibility choice.

options.title: Adopt shared 16 KiB limit
options.body: Merge the PR as written, aligning APNs with other bounded credential-file readers while preserving normal key and link layouts.

options.title: Choose an APNs-specific limit
options.body: Keep the shared helper but pass a larger explicit APNs maximum and add boundary coverage if maintainers want more compatibility headroom.

options.title: Keep unbounded reads
options.body: Decline the hardening and retain current behavior for all existing file sizes.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared 16 KiB limit
recommendation.body: Merge the PR as written, aligning APNs with other bounded credential-file readers while preserving normal key and link layouts.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged feature history ties the direct APNs signing configuration most directly to this person.
